recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed unless a future standards-status redesign intentionally changes the documentation index flag convention again.
issue_request: FHIR-14860 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core documentation clarification asking for guidance for the unexplained documentation status symbol. The accepted resolution was to provide a small legend at the bottom and flyover text for the symbols.
initial_application: Historical commit cb22f4aaf735c36bc02649580b3b70146519fd24, 'GF#14860 - explain [n] symbol', applied the issue by adding title="Normative Content" hover text to N flag anchors in source/documentation.html and a bottom note explaining the N symbol.
additional_context: Later R6 source commit 270e0ceb7b029dad4ca0fc5ccf5296ff370888cd changed the documentation index from N/normative markers to I/informative markers while preserving the guidance pattern. Current source/documentation.html has 28 informative flags, no normative flags, no flag anchors missing title text, and a bottom note explaining the I symbol. Community searches found only bot notifications and no Confluence references that would change the conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already satisfies the issue in the page's current standards-status vocabulary: the flag has title="Informative Content" flyover text and the note at the bottom explains what the I symbol means.
